text: Here's a maths problem.
Mia has three times as many marbles as Ben.
sub: Mia has *3 times* as many marbles as Ben.

text: Together, they have twenty-four. How many does Ben have?
sub: Together, they have *24*. How many does Ben have?

text: Tricky? Not the SAM way.
Step one. Make it real.
One block for Ben. Three blocks for Mia.
sub: *1 block* for Ben. *3 blocks* for Mia.

text: Every block is the same size. That's the secret.
sub: Every block is the *same size*. That's the secret.

text: Step two. Draw a picture.
Each block becomes a bar. We call it a unit.
sub: Each block becomes a bar. We call it a *unit*.

text: All the units together make twenty-four.
Step three. Now the numbers.
Four units make twenty-four.
So one unit is six.
Ben has six marbles. Mia has eighteen.
Concrete. Pictorial. Abstract. That's how Singapore teaches maths.
